sentences.text:
Order 
This is sixth bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail.
All five bail applications have been dismissed as withdrawn.

2. The applicant has been arrested on 27.04.2024 in connection with Crime No.131/2024 registered at Police Station - Bhonti, District Shivpuri for offence under Section 363, 376-D, 342, 376(2) (N),
328, 346 of IPC.
3. Prosecution story, in short is that the prosecutrix on 25.04.2024 orally stated that on 20.01.2024,she along with one Kunja had gone to Picchore Market to buy some gift.
There she went for some refreshment and after that she lost her consciousness and when she regained her consciousness, she found her self in a room.

The allegation is that the present applicant along with other co-accused persons abducted, kept her in different NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:17096 2 MCRC-21590-2025 places and committed repeatedly rape with her.
Then, she found a cell phone and called her mother.

Thereafter she was recovered from Jhansi,
(UP).
Accordingly, the offence has been registered.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant contended that the applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this matter.
He is in custody since 27.04.2024.

The alleged incident took place between 20.01.2024 and 22.04.2024 and the prosecutrix was allegedly recovered on 22.04.2024 still the FIR has been lodged on 24.05.2024 i.e. belatedly after three days.
The concerned Doctor (PW-5) has categorically admitted that no signs of injury as well as rape have been found on the body of the prosecutrix.
The applicant is a young boy aged 20 years.
Investigation is almost over in respect of applicant.

The applicant is permanent resident of District Shivpuri, therefore, custodial Anand Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64962753/
1 interrogation is no more required.

sentences.text: Final conclusion of trial will take time.
Hence, he prays that applicant be released on bail.
5. Per contra, learned PP for respondent/State opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.
6. Both the parties heard and perused the Case Diary.

7. Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by counsel for the parties, and also taking note of the facts that the applicant is in custody since 27.04.2024 and also taking note of the statement of doctor (PW-5) and final conclusion of trial will take long time

,
therefore, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:17096 3 MCRC-21590-2025 8.
Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by the conditions enumerated u/S. 437(3) Cr.P.C./480(3) of BNSS.
9.
